externalChannels.guideTitle: Create and configure your Slack App
externalChannels.guideDescription: Choose either method below. Both produce the same dedicated Slack App settings.
externalChannels.manifestIntro: Recommended: let Slack configure the bot, permissions, events, and callback from this generated manifest.
externalChannels.manifestStep1: Open Slack API → Your Apps → Create New App → From an app manifest.
externalChannels.manifestStep2: Choose the workspace where this Agent will be used.
externalChannels.manifestStep3: Copy the JSON below, paste it into Slack, review the summary, and create the App.
externalChannels.manifestStep4: Open OAuth & Permissions and select Install to Workspace.
externalChannels.manualIntro: Use these steps if you prefer to configure every setting directly in Slack.
externalChannels.manualStep1: Open Slack API → Your Apps → Create New App → From scratch, then choose the workspace.
externalChannels.manualStep2: Open OAuth & Permissions → Scopes → Bot Token Scopes and add every scope below.
externalChannels.manualHttpStep: Open Event Subscriptions, enable events, paste the Request URL below, then add every Bot Event listed below.
externalChannels.manualInteractivityStep: Open Interactivity & Shortcuts, turn Interactivity on, paste the same Request URL, and select Save Changes. Button clicks are not delivered without this setting.
externalChannels.manualSocketEventsStep: Open Event Subscriptions, enable events, then add every Bot Event listed below.
externalChannels.manualSocketStep: Open Socket Mode and enable it. Then open Basic Information → App-Level Tokens, generate a token with connections:write, and keep the xapp- token for the App-Level Token field below.
externalChannels.manualInstallStep: Open OAuth & Permissions and select Install to Workspace. If scopes change later, select Reinstall to Workspace.
externalChannels.manualInviteStep: In each target Slack channel, invite the bot with /invite @your-bot-name.
externalChannels.existingAppInteractivityTitle: Existing Slack Apps require an Interactivity update
externalChannels.existingAppInteractivityDescription: For an App created before conversation controls were added, open Interactivity & Shortcuts, turn Interactivity on, set this Request URL, and save the change.
externalChannels.reinstallNotice: Slack does not apply changed scopes until the App is reinstalled to the workspace.
externalChannels.credentialLocationsDescription: The fields below are different values. Copy each one from its exact Slack screen.
externalChannels.appIdLocation: App ID — Basic Information → App Credentials → App ID.
externalChannels.signingSecretLocation: Signing Secret — Basic Information → App Credentials → Signing Secret.
externalChannels.botTokenLocation: Bot User OAuth Token — OAuth & Permissions → OAuth Tokens for Your Workspace. It starts with xoxb- after installation.
externalChannels.appTokenLocation: App-Level Token — Basic Information → App-Level Tokens. Generate it with connections:write; it starts with xapp-.
externalChannels.tokenPrefixes: Never paste a User OAuth Token. Bot tokens start with xoxb-; Socket Mode App-Level Tokens start with xapp-.
externalChannels.credentialSafety: Credential values are encrypted by the server and are never shown again.
externalChannels.discordGuideCreateApplication: In Discord Developer Portal, open Applications → New Application. Create the App, then choose Bot → Add Bot from the left navigation. If the App already has a Bot, continue to the next step.
externalChannels.discordGuideEnableIntent: On the Bot page, enable the item below under Privileged Gateway Intents and select Save Changes. Without it, follow-up messages that do not mention the Bot may appear to be missing.
externalChannels.discordGuideCopyIdentifiers: Copy the Application ID from General Information. In Discord, enable User Settings → Advanced → Developer Mode, right-click the target server, and select Copy Server ID for the Guild ID. On the Bot page, use Reset Token to issue the Bot Token and keep it secure.
externalChannels.discordGuideConfigureOAuth: Under OAuth2 → URL Generator, select all of the following Scopes.
externalChannels.discordGuideGrantBotPermissions: Under Bot Permissions, select every permission listed below. Open the generated URL and add the Bot to the target server.
externalChannels.discordGuideVerifyChannelPermissions: For every channel the Bot will use, open Edit Channel → Permissions and confirm that the Bot role has the permissions below. If the channel inherits from a category, also check the category for explicit Deny rules.
externalChannels.discordGuideFinishSetup: Paste the Application ID, Guild ID, and Bot Token below and select Connect. Azents verifies the App and server identities, commands, interaction callback, and Gateway connection.
externalChannels.discordGuideLeastPrivilegeNote: The Bot does not need Administrator or Manage Messages. Do not enable Presence Intent or Server Members Intent. A channel or category Deny can override permissions granted to the server role.

github.runtimeEnvironmentWarningTitle: Runtime environment variables — long-lived credential risk
github.runtimeEnvironmentWarningBody: When enabled, GitHub tokens are injected into the agent runtime environment. Single-installation credentials also set GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN; multi-installation credentials set GITHUB_TOKEN_INSTALLATION_<id> plus a routing map used by the git credential helper. Full isolation is not possible — tokens can be read by any process the agent runs. Only enable if you accept this exposure risk.
github.runtimeEnvironmentToggle: Inject GitHub tokens into Runtime environment variables
github.runtimeEnvironmentToggleDescription: Requires acknowledgement above. Agents gain auto-auth for git commands. For gh commands with multi-installation credentials, use explicit token selection such as GH_TOKEN=$GITHUB_TOKEN_INSTALLATION_<id> gh ...
github.installationsDescription: Add every GitHub App installation this toolkit may use. The account login is used for tool prefixes and shell token routing.
github.reconnectReasonAppIdentityChanged: The instance Platform GitHub App changed. Reconnect this toolkit and save the refreshed installations before using it again.

slackApps.slackGuideTitle: Create and configure your Slack Multi App
slackApps.slackGuideStep1: Open Slack API → Your Apps and create an App from a manifest or from scratch for this Workspace.
slackApps.slackGuideStep2: Configure the Bot Token Scopes, Event Subscriptions, and either HTTP callbacks or Socket Mode for the selected transport.
slackApps.slackGuideStep3: Install or reinstall the App to the Slack Workspace, then copy the App ID, Bot Token, Signing Secret, and Socket Mode App Token when used.
slackApps.slackGuideStep4: Invite the bot to every target channel after connection so the App can receive and route messages.
slackApps.discordGuideTitle: Create and configure your Discord Multi App
slackApps.discordGuideStep1: Open Discord Developer Portal, create an Application, and create or reset its Bot Token.
slackApps.discordGuideStep2: Copy the Application ID and the target server's Guild ID with Discord Developer Mode enabled.
slackApps.discordGuideStep3: Enable the Gateway intents required by the App, then use OAuth2 URL Generator to add the bot to the target Guild.
slackApps.discordGuideStep4: Grant the bot the channel permissions needed for its intended conversations.
slackApps.discordGuideStep5: Submit the Application ID, Guild ID, and Bot Token below. Azents configures and verifies the interaction callback automatically.

integrations.discordGuide: Complete these steps in Discord Developer Portal, then enter the three values below. Azents validates the Bot Token and configures the interaction callback and commands automatically.
integrations.discordGuideCreateApplication: In Discord Developer Portal, open Applications → New Application. Create the App, then choose Bot → Add Bot from the left navigation. If the App already has a Bot, continue to the next step.
integrations.discordGuideEnableIntent: On the Bot page, enable the item below under Privileged Gateway Intents and select Save Changes. Without it, follow-up messages that do not mention the Bot may appear to be missing.
integrations.discordGuideCopyIdentifiers: Copy the Application ID from General Information. In Discord, enable User Settings → Advanced → Developer Mode, right-click the target server, and select Copy Server ID for the Guild ID. On the Bot page, use Reset Token to issue the Bot Token and keep it secure.
integrations.discordGuideConfigureOAuth: Under OAuth2 → URL Generator, select all of the following Scopes.
integrations.discordGuideGrantBotPermissions: Under Bot Permissions, select every permission listed below. Open the generated URL and add the Bot to the target server.
integrations.discordGuideVerifyChannelPermissions: For every channel the Bot will use, open Edit Channel → Permissions and confirm that the Bot role has the permissions below. If the channel inherits from a category, also check the category for explicit Deny rules.
integrations.discordGuideFinishSetup: Paste the Application ID, Guild ID, and Bot Token below and select Connect. Azents verifies the App and server identities, commands, interaction callback, and Gateway connection.
integrations.discordGuideLeastPrivilegeNote: The Bot does not need Administrator or Manage Messages. Do not enable Presence Intent or Server Members Intent. A channel or category Deny can override permissions granted to the server role.
